cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
Knowledge of or experience working within a complex, multi-disciplinary organization or higher education environment.
Experience coordinating administrative, operational, and logistical activities in support of programs, communications, events, or fundraising initiatives.
Experience conducting research and analysis using databases, CRM systems, donor management systems, or online information resources.
Experience utilizing financial, purchasing, travel, reimbursement, or related operational systems and processes.
Experience preparing correspondence, reports, presentations, acknowledgements, mail merges, and other professional communication materials.

Under the general direction of the Arts and Humanities Development Team, the Development Associate, Arts & Humanities provides administrative, operational, and programmatic support for alumni engagement, donor relations, and fundraising activities. The role coordinates logistics and operational processes related to virtual and in-person events, communications, annual giving initiatives, donor stewardship activities, and departmental campaigns.
Prospect Analysis and Advancement Support - 25%

The position supports the daily operations of the development team by managing scheduling, travel and entertainment arrangements, purchasing and reimbursement processes, vendor coordination, donor and alumni data maintenance, communications support, and event administration. The role also assists with gift processing support functions, donor acknowledgment activities, prospect research, and maintenance of donor records and engagement data within campus systems and databases.

Pull data reports from CADS and other research-related sources for alumni populations based on demographics, capacity to give, giving history, career, and other categories. Develop list criteria, prepare and curate constituency lists for programs, centers, newsletters, events, etc. Maintain and generate automated gift reports to A&H departments and centers.

The position works collaboratively with development staff, campus partners, alumni, donors, faculty, volunteers, students, and external stakeholders to support engagement and fundraising objectives. The role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, effective communication, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, customer service-oriented environment while ensuring compliance with campus policies, procedures, and operational guidelines.
Prepare donor briefings for frontline fundraisers and Deans donor meetings. Track on and be knowledgeable about constituent strategies, current engagement, preferences, and next steps.

Support the Division with Big Give, Crowdfunding, and other annual fund and giving campaigns by providing the departments, centers, and programs within the Division with the relevant background information to successfully participate in these campaigns. Support select gift operations efforts e.g. issues related to pledge fulfillment, gift misallocations/adjustments, complex donor and gift question trafficking, claiming wires, etc
Cultivation and Stewardship Programs - 25%

Manage the division's gift acknowledgement process, to include organizing, tracking, drafting and editing high-touch letters and sending timely correspondence. Templates are based on the voice of leadership, attending closely to the donors interests, their giving, and the donors relationship(s) on campus.

Support the team's stewardship projects such as organizing donor visits to departmental events/performances and implementing donor recognition projects. Maintain inventory of donor gifts, holiday cards, parking passes, event ticket purchases and office supplies through Bear Buy and/or special vendors.

Help support alumni relations, development and stewardship events for the team by calendaring, securing space and catering, and managing other logistical items related to the event. This may include preparing an invitation list, drafting an invitation, tracking RSVPs, preparing event materials (nametags, programs, host gifts, etc.), staff event, post-event tasks (reimbursements, thank you notes, etc).

Develop and support systems that operationalize Dean and Assistant Deans donor meetings, tasks, and follow ups. Plan, coordinate and execute donor visits and meetings, including drafting agendas, organizing and gathering content.

Support team operations, such as: overseeing the teams fulfillment program, paying invoices, ordering office supplies, answering and triaging incoming calls, greeting visitors, and providing occasional back up for executive assistants duties.
Assist in the development of proposals, presentations, site visits, board meetings, and other special events to meet key fundraising objectives.

Draft and edit a range of custom materials important to advancing relationships with high-level donors and prospects. Materials may include researching for proposals, suggested talking points, unique stewardship reports and materials, presentations with data and graphics, other external facing content on the divisional web site, and correspondence on behalf of campus leaders. Ensure accuracy of all written pieces.
Demonstrated proficiency with grammar, syntax, punctuation, and professional business writing standards.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Google Workspace, Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other relevant business software and systems.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to support strategic donor engagement and development operations.
Excellent written communication, editing, and research skills, including the ability to present complex information clearly for diverse audiences.
Outstanding organizational, project management, and multitasking skills with exceptional attention to detail, accuracy, and follow-through.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and achieve operational and programmatic goals in a fast-paced environment.
Strong customer service orientation and ability to provide professional support in a high-volume environment.
Excellent oral, interpersonal, and active listening skills, including political acumen and professionalism when interacting with stakeholders at all levels.
Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues, faculty, students, alumni, donors, volunteers, and campus partners.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a high-performing team with diverse responsibilities and priorities.
Demonstrated tact, discretion, sound judgment, and ability to maintain confidentiality with sensitive information and donor records.
Ability to professionally represent the department and development team at meetings, events, and donor engagement activities.
Working knowledge of policy interpretation, policy analysis techniques, and administrative procedures.
Ability to learn, interpret, and apply organizational policies, procedures, and operational guidelines.
Ability to learn and effectively utilize technology platforms, communication tools, and operational systems.

pay.source_text: ience. The budgeted hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $38.31 - $46.93. This is a non-exempt, bi-weekly paid position. This is a full-time (40 hours/week) Career position
